marks.gloss_en: דתניא... וחכמים אומרים: הכל הולך אחר המעמיד (kind tanya_kevatei: no kind names a bare דתניא)
with a hanging-board, follow its nails
לצדדים קתני -- with a seal, a man's ornament; without, a woman's: the Kelim mishna lists the sealed ring as an ornament, not as a woman's (= p_rava_litzedadim)
Rava: [the Kelim mishna] teaches the cases separately

טומאה אשבת קרמית?! -- impurity turns on 'a vessel of work', Shabbat on burden: the sealed ring is a vessel for impurity and a burden for Shabbat (= p_tumah_kli_maaseh, p_shabbat_mishum_masoi, p_yesh_chotam_masoi)
impurity: the Merciful One said 'a vessel of work', and it is a vessel
למאי חזיא? -- what is an unperforated needle fit for?
הואיל ואשה אוגרת בה שערה (= p_ogeret_bah_seara; felled at 60a.5)
the mishnah: [a woman may not go out on Shabbat] with a needle that is not perforated
אלא תרגמה רב אדא נרשאה קמיה דרב יוסף: הואיל ואשה חולקת בה שערה (= p_choleket_bah_seara)
בשבת למאי חזיא? -- on Shabbat, what is it fit for?
טס של זהב יש לה על ראשה... בשבת מניחתה כנגד פדחתה (= p_tas_shel_zahav)
Rav Adda Narshaah: since a woman parts her hair with it
אמר ליה אביי: ותהוי כבירית טהורה ותשתרי -- on your account it should be like a pure garter, and be permitted
Abaye: then let it be like a pure garter, and be permitted
אי הכי, בחול נמי ליתסר! -- if [the decree commemorates the incident], let it be forbidden on a weekday too
מעשה כי הוה בשבת הוה (= p_maaseh_beshabbat)
ביום טוב לישתרי! אלמה תנן: משלחין כלים ביום טוב ... אבל לא סנדל המסומר
at that hour they said: a person shall not go out in a spiked sandal
a man may not go out [on Shabbat] in a spiked sandal

Shmuel: fugitives from the persecution hid in a cave and said who enters may enter and who leaves may not leave; one man's sandal was reversed, they thought one had gone out and been seen by the enemy, and they crushed one another and killed more of themselves than the enemies had
R' Ilai ben Elazar: they were sitting in a cave and heard a sound from above the cave; they thought enemies had come upon them, crushed one another and killed one another
Rami bar Yechezkel: they were sitting in a synagogue and heard a sound from behind the synagogue; they thought enemies had come upon them, crushed one another and killed one another
